artifacts.summary: Root-cause analysis of the MT-1/MT-4 session-id mismatch in skill-orchestrate/SKILL.md that self-contends the task lock on every multi-task /orchestrate dispatch, with a minimal fix, a secondary heartbeat-consistency fix, and a concrete regression-test design.

next_steps: Run /plan 1008 to create an implementation plan: (1) change SKILL.md:1960 and SKILL.md:2388 from "${session_id}_${task_num}" to "$session_id" so Stage MT-4's task-lock acquire/release matches Stage MT-1's session-register and Stage MT-3's batch-admit calls; (2) change SKILL.md:2002's implement_agents dispatch context session_id to the bare $session_id so general-implementation-agent.md's phase-transition heartbeat keeps matching the lock holder; (3) add the MT-1->MT-4 end-to-end regression group to agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/test-conflict-predicate.sh as designed in the report's Recommendations section 4.

memory_candidates.content: task-lock.sh's session-registry contention pass (session_contention() in lib/file-scope-overlap.sh) self-excludes a registered session via an EXACT string match between the acquiring call's session_id argument and the session-register call's session_id argument (D4 exclusion 1). Any multi-task consumer that registers under one session_id form (e.g. a bare batch session_id) and later calls task-lock.sh acquire/release/heartbeat under a DIFFERENT form (e.g. a per-task-suffixed session_id) will have its own batch registration treated as a foreign, live, overlapping session on every acquire, since the registered file_scope is the union of every task's scope and therefore always overlaps each individual task's own scope. This produces a total, deterministic self-contention (not intermittent), and is a general trap for any future multi-task/batch consumer of task-lock.sh's session-registry CLI, not unique to skill-orchestrate.

In skill-orchestrate/SKILL.md's multi-task mode, the same session_id value flows into two independent purposes: (a) task-lock ownership identity (session-register at MT-1, acquire/release at MT-4, and downstream general-implementation-agent.md's phase-transition heartbeat, which reuses whatever session_id its own dispatch context carried) and (b) provenance/attribution metadata (skill_preflight_update/postflight_update, git-commit-scoped.sh --session, system-defect-record.sh --session), where per-task-suffixed uniqueness is harmless or even useful for log readability. When fixing a session-id mismatch bug, only the (a)-class call sites need to agree on one exact string; (b)-class call sites can safely keep a per-task-suffixed convention. Conflating the two, or fixing only some of the (a)-class sites, is the recurring failure mode.
